source.title: Belfast Newsletter, 17 May 1961, p. 5 ("Nominations for councils: Two nominations for Holywood seat")
source.publisher: Belfast Newsletter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: returned unopposed: '21 nominations for the 20 divisional seats' with Holywood the only contest, and 'Mr. F. C. Tughan, former Mayor of Bangor, has been nominated to succeed Mr. F. Logan who is retiring after having represented Bangor for almost 10 years' (Belfast Newsletter, 17 May 1961, p. 5)

note: Polled 1 June 1961 (Belfast Telegraph, 31 May 1961, Down County Council election advertisement: 'TAKES PLACE 1st JUNE'). Holywood was the only division contested: William Mawhinney (Unionist) 3,742 beat W. P. N. Dunn (Unionist) 2,621. The Belfast Newsletter of 17 May 1961, p. 5, has '21 nominations for the 20 divisional seats' and names the two new members (Bangor, Garvaghy); the Lisburn Herald of 20 May 1961, p. 3, names Hillsborough and Saintfield. Three more divisions (Ballynahinch, Rathfryland, Portaferry) are recorded from reports of the new council's meetings; the other twelve are not recorded (meetings pass, 7 Nov 2026). The 1964 notice of result gives the same member in full as Frederick C. Tughan. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
